layout_dets.text: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Image Segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Olaf Ronneberger, Philipp Fischer, and Thomas Brox

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Computer Science Department and BIOSS Centre for Biological Signalling Studies,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: University of Freiburg, Germany

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ronneber@informatik.uni-freiburg.de,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: WWW home page: http://1mb.informatik.uni-freiburg.de/

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract. There is large consent that successful training of deep net-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: works requires many thousand annotated training samples. In this pa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: per, we present a network and training strategy that relies on the strong

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: use of data augmentation to use the available annotated samples more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: efficiently. The architecture consists of a contracting path to capture

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: context and a symmetric expanding path that enables precise localiza-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion. We show that such a network can be trained end-to-end from very

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: few images and outperforms the prior best method (a sliding-window

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: convolutional network) on the ISBI challenge for segmentation of neu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ronal structures in electron microscopic stacks. Using the same net-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: work trained on transmitted light microscopy images (phase contrast

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and DIC) we won the ISBI cell tracking challenge 2015 in these cate-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gories by a large margin. Moreover, the network is fast. Segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of a 512x512 image takes less than a second on a recent GPU. The full

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: implementation (based on Caffe) and the trained networks are available

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at http://lmb.informatik.uni-freiburg.de/people/ronneber/u-net.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1 Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the last two years, deep convolutional networks have outperformed the state of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the art in many visual recognition tasks, e.g. [7,3]. While convolutional networks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have already existed for a long time [8], their success was limited due to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: size of the available training sets and the size of the considered networks. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: breakthrough by Krizhevsky et al. [7] was due to supervised training of a large

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: network with 8 layers and millions of parameters on the ImageNet dataset with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1 million training images. Since then, even larger and deeper networks have been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trained [12].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The typical use of convolutional networks is on classification tasks, where

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the output to an image is a single class label. However, in many visual tasks,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: especially in biomedical image processing, the desired output should include

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: localization, i.e., a class label is supposed to be assigned to each pixel. More-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: over, thousands of training images are usually beyond reach in biomedical tasks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hence, Ciresan et al. [1] trained a network in a sliding-window setup to predict

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the class label of each pixel by providing a local region (patch) around that pixel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 1. U-net architecture (example for 32x32 pixels in the lowest resolution). Each blue

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: box corresponds to a multi-channel feature map. The number of channels is denoted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on top of the box. The x-y-size is provided at the lower left edge of the box. White

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: boxes represent copied feature maps. The arrows denote the different operations.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as input. First, this network can localize. Secondly, the training data in terms

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of patches is much larger than the number of training images. The resulting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: network won the EM segmentation challenge at ISBI 2012 by a large margin

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Obviously, the strategy in Ciresan et al. [1] has two drawbacks. First, it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is quite slow because the network must be run separately for each patch, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: there is a lot of redundancy due to overlapping patches. Secondly, there is a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trade-off between localization accuracy and the use of context. Larger patches

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: require more max-pooling layers that reduce the localization accuracy, while

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: small patches allow the network to see only little context. More recent approaches

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [11,4] proposed a classifier output that takes into account the features from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: multiple layers. Good localization and the use of context are possible at the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: same time.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, we build upon a more elegant architecture, the so-called "fully

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: convolutional network" [9]. We modify and extend this architecture such that it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: works with very few training images and yields more precise segmentations; see

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 1. The main idea in [9] is to supplement a usual contracting network by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: successive layers, where pooling operators are replaced by upsampling operators.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hence, these layers increase the resolution of the output. In order to localize, high

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resolution features from the contracting path are combined with the upsampled

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 2. Overlap-tile strategy for seamless segmentation of arbitrary large images (here

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation of neuronal structures in EM stacks). Prediction of the segmentation in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the yellow area, requires image data within the blue area as input. Missing input data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is extrapolated by mirroring

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: output. A successive convolution layer can then learn to assemble a more precise

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: output based on this information.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: One important modification in our architecture is that in the upsampling

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: part we have also a large number of feature channels, which allow the network

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to propagate context information to higher resolution layers. As a consequence,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the expansive path is more or less symmetric to the contracting path, and yields

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a u-shaped architecture. The network does not have any fully connected layers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and only uses the valid part of each convolution, i.e., the segmentation map only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contains the pixels, for which the full context is available in the input image.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This strategy allows the seamless segmentation of arbitrarily large images by an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: overlap-tile strategy (see Figure 2). To predict the pixels in the border region

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the image, the missing context is extrapolated by mirroring the input image.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This tiling strategy is important to apply the network to large images, since

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: otherwise the resolution would be limited by the GPU memory.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As for our tasks there is very little training data available, we use excessive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: data augmentation by applying elastic deformations to the available training im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ages. This allows the network to learn invariance to such deformations, without

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the need to see these transformations in the annotated image corpus. This is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: particularly important in biomedical segmentation, since deformation used to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be the most common variation in tissue and realistic deformations can be simu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lated efficiently. The value of data augmentation for learning invariance has been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shown in Dosovitskiy et al. [2] in the scope of unsupervised feature learning.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Another challenge in many cell segmentation tasks is the separation of touch-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing objects of the same class; see Figure 3. To this end, we propose the use of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a weighted loss, where the separating background labels between touching cells

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: obtain a large weight in the loss function.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The resulting network is applicable to various biomedical segmentation prob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lems. In this paper, we show results on the segmentation of neuronal structures

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in EM stacks (an ongoing competition started at ISBI 2012), where we out-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performed the network of Ciresan et al. [1]. Furthermore, we show results for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cell segmentation in light microscopy images from the ISBI cell tracking chal-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lenge 2015. Here we won with a large margin on the two most challenging 2D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transmitted light datasets.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2 Network Architecture

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The network architecture is illustrated in Figure 1. It consists of a contracting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: path (left side) and an expansive path (right side). The contracting path follows

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the typical architecture of a convolutional network. It consists of the repeated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: application of two 3x3 convolutions (unpadded convolutions), each followed by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a rectified linear unit (ReLU) and a 2x2 max pooling operation with stride 2

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for downsampling. At each downsampling step we double the number of feature

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: channels. Every step in the expansive path consists of an upsampling of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: feature map followed by a 2x2 convolution (“up-convolution") that halves the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: number of feature channels, a concatenation with the correspondingly cropped

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: feature map from the contracting path, and two 3x3 convolutions, each fol-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lowed by a ReLU. The cropping is necessary due to the loss of border pixels in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: every convolution. At the final layer a 1x1 convolution is used to map each 64-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: component feature vector to the desired number of classes. In total the network

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has 23 convolutional layers.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To allow a seamless tiling of the output segmentation map (see Figure 2), it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is important to select the input tile size such that all 2x2 max-pooling operations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are applied to a layer with an even x- and y-size.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3 Training

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The input images and their corresponding segmentation maps are used to train

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the network with the stochastic gradient descent implementation of Caffe [6].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Due to the unpadded convolutions, the output image is smaller than the input

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by a constant border width. To minimize the overhead and make maximum use

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the GPU memory, we favor large input tiles over a large batch size and hence

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reduce the batch to a single image. Accordingly we use a high momentum (0.99)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: such that a large number of the previously seen training samples determine the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: update in the current optimization step.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The energy function is computed by a pixel-wise soft-max over the final

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: feature map combined with the cross entropy loss function. The soft-max is

layout_dets.text: 3.1 Data Augmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Data augmentation is essential to teach the network the desired invariance and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: robustness properties, when only few training samples are available. In case of

layout_dets.text: microscopical images we primarily need shift and rotation invariance as well as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: robustness to deformations and gray value variations. Especially random elas-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tic deformations of the training samples seem to be the key concept to train

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a segmentation network with very few annotated images. We generate smooth

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deformations using random displacement vectors on a coarse 3 by 3 grid. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: displacements are sampled from a Gaussian distribution with 10 pixels standard

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deviation. Per-pixel displacements are then computed using bicubic interpola-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion. Drop-out layers at the end of the contracting path perform further implicit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: data augmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4 Experiments

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We demonstrate the application of the u-net to three different segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tasks. The first task is the segmentation of neuronal structures in electron mi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: croscopic recordings. An example of the data set and our obtained segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is displayed in Figure 2. We provide the full result as Supplementary Material

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The data set is provided by the EM segmentation challenge [14] that was started

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at ISBI 2012 and is still open for new contributions. The training data is a set of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 30 images (512x512 pixels) from serial section transmission electron microscopy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the Drosophila first instar larva ventral nerve cord (VNC). Each image comes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with a corresponding fully annotated ground truth segmentation map for cells

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (white) and membranes (black). The test set is publicly available, but its seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation maps are kept secret. An evaluation can be obtained by sending the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: predicted membrane probability map to the organizers. The evaluation is done

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by thresholding the map at 10 different levels and computation of the "warping

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: error", the “Rand error" and the “pixel error" [14].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The u-net (averaged over 7 rotated versions of the input data) achieves with-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: out any further pre- or postprocessing a warping error of 0.0003529 (the new

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: best score, see Table 1) and a rand-error of 0.0382.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This is significantly better than the sliding-window convolutional network

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: result by Ciresan et al. [1], whose best submission had a warping error of 0.000420

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and a rand error of 0.0504. In terms of rand error the only better performing

layout_dets.text: We also applied the u-net to a cell segmentation task in light microscopic im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ages. This segmenation task is part of the ISBI cell tracking challenge 2014 and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2015 [10,13]. The first data set "PhC-U373"2 contains Glioblastoma-astrocytoma

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: U373 cells on a polyacrylimide substrate recorded by phase contrast microscopy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (see Figure 4a,b and Supp. Material). It contains 35 partially annotated train-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing images. Here we achieve an average IOU (“intersection over union") of 92%,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which is significantly better than the second best algorithm with 83% (see Ta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ble 2). The second data set “DIC-HeLa"3 are HeLa cells on a flat glass recorded

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by differential interference contrast (DIC) microscopy (see Figure 3, Figure 4c,d

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and Supp. Material). It contains 20 partially annotated training images. Here we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: achieve an average IOU of 77.5% which is significantly better than the second

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: best algorithm with 46%.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5 Conclusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The u-net architecture achieves very good performance on very different biomed-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ical segmentation applications. Thanks to data augmentation with elastic defor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The Netherlands

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mations, it only needs very few annotated images and has a very reasonable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training time of only 10 hours on a NVidia Titan GPU (6 GB). We provide the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: full Caffe[6]-based implementation and the trained networks4. We are sure that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the u-net architecture can be applied easily to many more tasks.
